auth_module_map.role: Defines AbstractBaseUser with password, last_login fields; BaseUserManager; core auth interfaces (set_password, check_password, has_usable_password, get_session_auth_hash)

Defines AbstractUser (extends AbstractBaseUser + PermissionsMixin) with username, email, first_name, last_name, is_staff, is_active, date_joined; PermissionsMixin with is_superuser, groups, user_permissions; concrete User model with swappable Meta
Initial migration defining User, Group, Permission models; establishes field schema for contrib.auth integration

migration_trace: Step 1: Review AbstractBaseUser definition (django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:43-165) - provides password field (line 44) and last_login DateTimeField (line 45)

Step 2: Review AbstractUser definition (django/contrib/auth/models.py:451-520) - adds username (line 461), first_name (line 473), last_name (line 474), email (line 475), is_staff (line 476), is_active (line 481), date_joined (line 489) on top of AbstractBaseUser + PermissionsMixin
Step 3: Review PermissionsMixin (django/contrib/auth/models.py:322-357) - adds is_superuser (line 328), groups M2M (line 336), user_permissions M2M (line 347)
Step 4: Review User concrete model (django/contrib/auth/models.py:522-532) - inherits from AbstractUser, sets swappable Meta (line 531) for AUTH_USER_MODEL customization
Step 5: Check initial migration (django/contrib/auth/migrations/0001_initial.py:81-150) - defines database schema for User model including all contrib.auth fields
Step 6: Identify unmappable custom fields - profile_tier, external_sso_id, last_sync_at have no direct correspondence in AbstractBaseUser or AbstractUser
Step 7: Plan migration strategy - migrate to AbstractBaseUser by creating custom User model that extends AbstractBaseUser, override USERNAME_FIELD, add unmappable fields to custom model

unmappable_fields.reason: CharField with choices (free/pro/enterprise) has no equivalent in AbstractBaseUser or AbstractUser. AbstractUser provides basic user attributes (first_name, last_name, email) but no tier/category field. PermissionsMixin uses groups for permissions, not tier classification.
unmappable_fields.migration_strategy: Add profile_tier as CharField with choices directly to custom User model extending AbstractBaseUser. Alternatively, create a separate UserProfile OneToOneField model for profile-specific attributes to maintain separation of concerns. Map existing data with data migration.
unmappable_fields.evidence: AbstractBaseUser (django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:43-45) contains only password + last_login; AbstractUser (django/contrib/auth/models.py:451-489) adds user identity fields but no tier field; PermissionsMixin (django/contrib/auth/models.py:328-354) uses groups/permissions, not tier

unmappable_fields.reason: CharField with unique=True constraint for SSO integration has no correspondence in contrib.auth. AbstractBaseUser and AbstractUser are designed for Django's built-in auth; external identity mapping is application-specific. No field in contrib.auth models addresses external system IDs.
unmappable_fields.migration_strategy: Add external_sso_id as CharField(unique=True, null=True, blank=True) directly to custom User model extending AbstractBaseUser. Create unique constraint in model Meta. Create data migration to backfill existing users. Consider adding a separate UserSSO model if needing to track multiple SSO providers per user.
unmappable_fields.evidence: AbstractBaseUser (django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:43-165) has no external identity field; AbstractUser (django/contrib/auth/models.py:451-520) focuses on username-based auth; no SSO or external ID support in PermissionsMixin

unmappable_fields.reason: DateTimeField for tracking last SSO/external system sync has no equivalent in contrib.auth. AbstractBaseUser provides last_login (line 45 in base_user.py) which tracks authentication login time, not system sync time. These are semantically different and serve different purposes.
unmappable_fields.migration_strategy: Add last_sync_at as DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True) directly to custom User model extending AbstractBaseUser. Keep last_login separate for its auth tracking purpose. Create data migration to initialize last_sync_at from last_login if applicable, or leave null for new sync-based workflows.
unmappable_fields.evidence: AbstractBaseUser.last_login (django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:45) is DateTimeField for auth tracking only; no sync-tracking field exists. In models.py:451-520 AbstractUser does not add sync-related fields. Signal handler (models.py:18-24) updates last_login on authentication, not on sync operations
